title: made a robotaxi game on real SF map with AI, can’t decide if it should be NFS or crazy taxi
author: marina_sd20
selftext:
so i’ve been working on this game called teleoperator. you’re basically a remote operator driving robotaxis around san francisco, picking up fares and trying not to wreck so you make money. you can drive a waymo, cybercab, cybertruck, ferrari or a corvette, because why not

it's fully vibecoded, the stack is fable + three.js, runs in the browser. it’s gotten over 20k plays since last week, which is super exciting, and now i'm kind of stuck on where to take it.

a lot of people on X said it reminds them of crazy taxi, and honestly i see it. part of me wants to lean all the way in, arcade chaos, combos, dumb stunts off the hills, etc., the other option is going more NFS: more cities, more cars, driving that feels real.

what direction would make you come back for the game? any ideas/feedback is very welcome!

game link: [mindblown.ai/games/teleoperator](http://mindblown.ai/games/teleoperator)

comments.author: ledniv
comments.body: How did you build the city?

replies.author: Intelligent-Cap-8886
replies.body: Rock and Roll.

replies.author: marina_sd20
replies.body: a lot of image and map references. i even tell it find various prominent sites in san francisco, take pictures then try to make it look similar in the game

replies.author: ledniv
replies.body: So you had it build the city by hand? You didn't use something like open street map data?

replies.author: RemarkableWish2508
replies.body: With web access, it may have pulled data from OpenStreetMap in the background.

replies.author: marina_sd20
replies.body: yep, openstreetmap is the base for the streets

comments.body: So it's just a taxi game if you peel off the Waymo narrative because there's nothing robotaxi about it.

replies.author: ArialBear
replies.body: What would make it robot taxi? Like auto steer power ups?

replies.author: marina_sd20

comments.author: Intelligent-Cap-8886
comments.body: What about if youre an Indian guy trying to drive a bunch of fake/crappy AI taxis preventing them from killing customers? :)

comments.author: i_rate_slop
comments.body: I’m disappointed that you appear to be manually driving

replies.author: marina_sd20
replies.body: do you think it would be better if the car drives itself, and you jump in when it gets confused or does something dumb?

replies.author: i_rate_slop
replies.body:
Oh, I have no idea. But it would be amusing if you could figure out a way to make auto driving fun. 

Only thing that comes to mind is Waymo temple run, but your starting point here is already better than any temple run style game.

replies.author: marina_sd20
replies.body: lol waymo temple run is kind of genius. thanks btw, appreciate it!

comments.author: Desperate_Source_712
comments.body: Need to watch ok out for car manufactures. See if you can be like gta and recreate own cars

replies.author: marina_sd20
replies.body: yeah good call! GTA-style parody cars are probably the move, and honestly more fun to design anyway

comments.author: luisbg
comments.body: Where did you get the 3d models for the cars and street furniture?

replies.author: DonkeyComfortable711
replies.body: tbh, if you have a lot of tokens to burn.  give your agent blender and a bunch of pictures and itll make it one to one.

replies.author: marina_sd20
replies.body: mostly AI-generated. the agent had blender and 3d model gen to work with, so it made the street furniture as reusable pieces that get placed around the city. cars too, except the ferrari, that one’s from the three.js demos

replies.author: luisbg
replies.body: Cool. I've never tried a Blender MCP.

replies.author: marina_sd20
replies.body: ha not an MCP actually, blender was already installed where the mindblown AI's game maker agent runs, so it used it directly

replies.author: marina_sd20
replies.body: that’s a great idea! if you were designing it, what would the core loop be? like are you dispatching cars to fares, fighting rival fleets, managing charging?

replies.author: Recoil42
replies.body: All of the above. :)

replies.author: marina_sd20
replies.body: ha the dream. but also a lot of token burn lol

replies.author: Recoil42
replies.body: Throw a prompt in and see what happens. It can be pretty surprising how low-burn an ambitious prompt can be when it's done one-shot.

comments.author: shizola_owns
comments.body: A real map doesn't lend itself well to crazy taxi gameplay. Where did you get the car models from?

replies.author: marina_sd20
replies.body: cars are mostly AI-generated. ferrari is the exception, that one’s from the three.js demos

comments.author: Jlocke98
comments.body: Gotta make it a roguelite with some mechanics for shoving other cars

replies.author: marina_sd20
replies.body: i love this. how would you see the roguelite part working?

replies.author: Jlocke98
replies.body: Similar gameplay loop as crazy taxi (timer going down but gets replenished by new customers) and different kinds of customers give different kinds of upgrades, with the quality/duration of upgrade being dependent on how well you drove or achieved some mini objective like not hitting any cars, or drifting a bunch, or destroying other cars in some fun way.

replies.author: marina_sd20
replies.body: this sounds great. thank you!

comments.author: Song-Historical
comments.body:
Would be cool to build in an AI swarm enemy. You're a teleoperator trying to keep the cars on track and picking up fares so the training goes well, and you keep your job. You're up against an AI that's bent on getting your contract. If you play dirty, take shortcuts, etc it plays dirty. If you want to chill and play by the rules, so does the AI. Occasionally police should try to pull you over if you're acting erratic. Put in some mini games about filing reports and some swarm management for your block of cars. Charging points and pit stops. 

Heck you could put a hubworld in there that's your office and then have different cities or just pointless watercooler talk, reports and bulletin boards. Maybe you throw in some sinister post its from a past employee. A password that gives you access to different conversations in the back of the car for an investigation. Maybe hackers take control of a swarm to assist with petty crime and corporate decides that's your problem to deal with, so you now have to track different routes and mark which ones are fake and which are normal rides.

So many things you could do.

replies.author: marina_sd20
replies.body: ok this totally changed how i was thinking about it. probably not going full dystopia with this one, but the rival AI that copies how you drive is such a cool idea, and the sinister post-its made me laugh. thanks for this!

replies.author: marina_sd20
replies.body: oh man midtown madness, that’s a great reference. midtown madness 2 even had san francisco, so that’s a pretty perfect comparison. what did you love most about it?
